title: POC scoping - success criteria signoff
summary: Redwood and Orion aligned on POC success criteria and acceptance tests. Agreed benchmark workloads, go/no-go thresholds for latency, throughput, and quality; reporting format (CSV + dashboard + summary slide); and a 2-week pilot timeline with a 3-day full-load benchmark as the gating evaluation. Action items assigned for test corpus, infra access, and pricing follow-up.

acceptance_tests: Functional: generated responses must match oracle labels >= 92% (per-token match or human eval agreement > 90%)
Latency: p50 < 150ms, p95 < 400ms for 512-token context during benchmark
Throughput: sustain 50 req/s with average concurrency of 12 without tail-latency spikes
Reliability: 99.5% success rate (no errors) across 3-day run
Cost: unit inference cost not exceeding agreed estimate (TBD in SOW)
Security: audit logs for all requests and encryption-at-rest with customer-managed KMS
benchmark_plan: Dataset: 20k-50k representative prompts + 2k edge-case prompts provided by customer
Phases: smoke test (1 day), functional benchmarks (2 days), full-load soak (3 days) - run window for full-load recommended in production-like infra
Metrics to capture: latency (p50/p95/p99), throughput (req/s), error-rate, model output quality (automated match + manual spot check), cost per token
Reporting: CSV export of raw metrics + prebuilt dashboard (Grafana/Looker) + executive summary slide deck
reporting_format: Raw CSV with per-request rows (timestamp, request_id, prompt_id, latency_ms, status_code, model_variant, token_count, cost_estimate)
Dashboard: per-route panels (latency percentiles, throughput, error rate) and a quality panel showing automated match rate
Summary: 1-page executive summary + 5-slide technical appendix describing test setup and outliers
timeline: Week 0 (by 2025-12-24): sign SOW and share sample data
Week 1 (2025-12-30): Redwood to provision test environment and run smoke tests
Week 2 (2026-01-06): 3-day full-load benchmark window + manual evals
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-12-20 15:00 PST | Duration: ~62 minutes | Attendees: Alex Chen, Priya Rao, Drew Martinez (Redwood) / Jordan Lee, Sana Patel, Marco Diaz, Lina Park (Orion)

[00:00] Alex: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda, align on success criteria, workload size, benchmarks and sign off on acceptance tests. 
[00:12] Jordan: yep, thanks. we had a quick sync internally, so want to make sure the POC actually proves latency and cost targets before we move to dedicated.
[00:20] Sana: and security obviously - audit logs and KMS are must-haves.
[00:25] Priya: totally. i'll go through the benchmark plan then we can walk thresholds and reporting.
[00:33] Priya: first, workload sizing. you said your production fan-out is around 40 rps currently during peak for the ranking service, correct?
[00:45] Jordan: right, 40 rps sustained with bursts to ~80 for a few minutes. most requests are short, ~128 tokens, but the reranker sometimes needs 512 tokens.
[00:58] Drew: ok so we'll test with a mix — 70% short prompts (128 tokens), 25% medium (256 tokens), 5% long (512 tokens). that should emulate your distribution.
[01:10] Jordan: sounds good. we can provide real sample prompts, about 20k-50k.
[01:18] Sana: and we have golden labels for the ranking outputs, about 10k labeled examples.
[01:24] Alex: perfect. acceptance tests i propose are a combination of quality + infra metrics. for quality we want automated match rate against your golden labels and a manual spot-check. we suggested >=92% automated match or human-eval agreement >90%.
[01:40] Lina: uh can you clarify automated match, is that token-for-token or semantic match?
[01:46] Priya: good question. the automated check will be a normalized string match on canonicalized outputs for the reranker scoring, plus a semantic similarity fallback. we'll include threshold rules in the report.
[01:58] Marco: on security, we need all requests logged with unique ids, and keys in our KMS. can you support customer-managed KMS?
[02:06] Alex: yes, our private deployment supports CMK via standard KMS/HSM integrations; for hosted we have options to integrate with BYOK — we'll include details in the security pack.
[02:20] Jordan: latency targets? we need p95 under 500ms today, but if you can demonstrate p95 under 400ms that would be great.
[02:30] Priya: we proposed p50 < 150ms and p95 < 400ms for 512-token context during the benchmark; that's achievable on our dedicated profile. note that p99 will be higher — we'll show that too.
[02:45] Jordan: and throughput? can you sustain 50 req/s for 3 days?
[02:50] Drew: yes, we'll run a soak targeting 50 req/s sustained with bursts to 80 — we'll watch tail latencies. the acceptance criteria will allow occasional brief spikes but overall p95 must remain under threshold.
[03:05] Sana: how will you measure quality at scale? we don't fully trust automated matching for open responses.
[03:12] Priya: agreed. plan is automated scoring for 100% of requests + a sampling manual review of ~200 responses each day during the full-load run. manual reviewers will rate pass/fail against acceptance rubric.
[03:25] Alex: and the final go/no-go decision is based on: 1) automated metrics meeting thresholds, 2) manual spot-check pass rate >90%, 3) no severe security gaps.
[03:37] Jordan: makes sense. about reporting format — we need raw CSVs as well as a dashboard.
[03:42] Priya: we'll provide per-request CSV (timestamp, id, prompt_id, latency_ms, model_variant, tokens, cost_estimate, status). plus a Grafana dashboard link and a summary slide deck with executive conclusion.
[03:56] Lina: for the cost gate, we need a rough estimate of per-request unit cost during the run to compare to our baseline.
[04:02] Alex: we'll provide cost estimates in the SOW; for the benchmark we'll report a cost burn table and projected steady-state unit cost.
[04:12] Marco: also need to confirm retention for logs and who has access.
[04:16] Alex: retention policy will be configurable; for the POC we'll store logs for 30 days with role-based access.
[04:24] Jordan: timeline? we'd like this done before our architecture review on Jan 15.
[04:29] Alex: propose sign SOW this week, smoke tests last week of December and full-run first week of Jan — that aligns.
[04:37] Priya: scheduling note — if you want a production-like network path we recommend running the soak from our dedicated pool in US-west because that's closest to your infra.
[04:48] Jordan: cool. are there any blockers from Redwood side?
[04:51] Priya: we'll need test credentials and the sample prompt set, and an allowlist IP/peering info if you want VPC peering.
[04:58] Sana: we'll get that to you by next Tuesday.
[05:02] Alex: ok, walk through acceptance test language for the SOW out loud so we have it on the call.
[05:08] Alex: acceptance test 1: quality — automated match >=92% on provided golden set or manual spot-check agreement >90%.
[05:16] Jordan: agreed.
[05:18] Alex: acceptance test 2: latency — measured p50 < 150ms, p95 < 400ms for 512 token context across the three-day run.
[05:26] Jordan: agreed.
[05:27] Alex: acceptance test 3: throughput — sustain 50 req/s for the soak with no more than 1% errors.
[05:34] Marco: 1% error seems fair. what counts as error? 5xxs and timeouts?
[05:38] Priya: yes 5xx, 504/timeout, or invalid responses that fail schema validation.
[05:44] Alex: acceptance test 4: security — audit log availability, encryption-at-rest with CMK and SSO/SCIM provisioned.
[05:52] Marco: for SSO we need SAML metadata and SCIM user provisioning for 10 test users.
[05:57] Alex: noted. we'll include a checklist in the security pack.
[06:02] Lina: if one threshold fails marginally, is there a remediation window?
[06:07] Alex: yes — for non-security or non-critical failures we allow a remediation window of 3 business days to rerun the benchmark. critical security failures cause immediate fail.
[06:18] Jordan: so decision rubric: pass all critical items or acceptable remediation plan within 3 days.
[06:24] Alex: exactly.
[06:26] Jordan: ok let's confirm outputs we'll get: raw CSV, dashboard link, cost table, executive summary slide, and access to logs (30d).
[06:34] Priya: plus the benchmark script and config so you can reproduce locally if needed.
[06:39] Sana: and we'll want to run a few internal queries on the raw CSV; what format will prompt ids use?
[06:44] Priya: we'll use your prompt_id field if you provide it, otherwise we'll generate stable uuids.
[06:51] Alex: final recap — Alex sends SOW + pricing; Sana provides data and keys; Redwood runs smoke tests then 3-day soak; report shared and decision by 2026-01-13.
[07:05] Jordan: thanks everyone — good alignment.
[07:10] Alex: thanks all, we'll follow up with action items in the next 24 hours.
